title: Given two lists of closed intervals each sorted by start and internally non-overlapping, return the list of intervals representing their intersection. Solve it with the two-pointer merge-intervals pattern and demonstrate with a complete banking mini-project.

s1_definition.oneliner: The overlap of two intervals is max-start to min-end; advance the pointer of whichever interval ends first.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Two-pointer scan** – walk both sorted lists simultaneously with one pointer each; no additional sorting needed.
- **Overlap formula** – the intersection of intervals a and b is [max(a.start, b.start), min(a.end, b.end)] if max-start <= min-end.
- **End-based advancement** – advance the pointer of the interval that ends earlier because it is exhausted and cannot overlap anything further.
- **Linear time** – O(m + n) where m and n are the list lengths; each pointer advances at most through its own list once.
- **No mutation** – build a fresh result list without modifying the inputs.
s1_definition.analogy: At National Bank of India, Rajesh has two sorted timelines: one of windows when an account was eligible for trading and one of windows when the market was open. He needs the windows when both conditions held. He walks both timelines together, taking the slice where they overlap, and steps forward on whichever window closes first.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
     Interval Intersection: Two-Pointer Scan

     List A: [0,2]  [5,10]  [13,23]  [24,25]
     List B: [1,5]  [8,12]  [15,24]  [25,26]

     Step 1: a=[0,2] b=[1,5]
       lo=max(0,1)=1  hi=min(2,5)=2  => [1,2]
       a ends first (2<5) => advance i

     Step 2: a=[5,10] b=[1,5]
       lo=max(5,1)=5  hi=min(10,5)=5  => [5,5]
       b ends first (5<10) => advance j

     Step 3: a=[5,10] b=[8,12]
       lo=max(5,8)=8  hi=min(10,12)=10  => [8,10]
       a ends first (10<12) => advance i

     Step 4: a=[13,23] b=[8,12]
       lo=max(13,8)=13  hi=min(23,12)=12  => 13>12, no overlap
       b ends first (12<23) => advance j

     ... continues until one list exhausted
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
The intervals intersection problem takes two sorted, non-overlapping lists and returns the list where they overlap. The solution is a two-pointer scan in O(m + n) time. At each step, compute the potential overlap as the later of the two starts to the earlier of the two ends. If that range is valid (start <= end), it is a real intersection.

The decision that makes the scan work is advancing the pointer of the interval that ends earlier. That interval is exhausted because it cannot overlap any later interval in the other list. Advancing based on the start instead of the end is the most common mistake and causes skipped overlaps.

At National Bank of India, the trading-window service uses this to find the exact windows when both account eligibility and market open-session conditions hold simultaneously. The two-pointer scan computes all tradeable windows in a single linear pass.

The senior-level insight is that this generalises to intersecting N sorted lists using a min-heap for the end-advance coordination. Explaining the max-start/min-end formula, the end-based advancement, and the generalisation to N lists is what tells an interviewer you own this technique.

Remember one sentence: overlap is max-start to min-end, advance the pointer of whichever interval ends first, and you get all intersections in linear time.

---

No sorting needed because both input lists are already sorted and internally non-overlapping.
